corpusSummary: Across a broad set of social-science studies, the corpus documents how large language models shape cognition, communication, and decision-making, while being scrutinized as study tools, educational aids, or policy actors. Findings highlight limitations in embodied knowledge, biases, and interpretive fidelity; opportunities include new methodologies, improved AI literacy, governance frameworks prioritizing equity, and nuanced insights into health, education, and public discourse.

themes.name: Socio-cognitive dynamics of LLMs
themes.description: Studies document how LLMs simulate personality, empathy, and social biases, shaping trust, decision-making, and the emergence of utopian or polarized social dynamics, with anthropomorphism, dependency, and sycophancy.

themes.name: LLMs as research tools and governance
themes.description: A growing strand treats LLMs as methodological aids for coding, analysis, simulations, and policy work, while calling for validation, transparency, and governance frameworks.

themes.name: AI in health and wellbeing
themes.description: Generative AI's role in health includes misinformation risk, patient education, clinical decision support, and equity considerations across diverse populations.

themes.name: AI in education and workforce development
themes.description: GenAI applications span tutoring, assessment, literacy, and pedagogy, with attention to AI readiness, dependence, teacher roles, and the digital divide.

themes.name: AI for public policy, climate, and media
themes.description: LLMs support sentiment analysis, urban planning deliberation, policy analysis, and journalistic practice, while raising concerns about reliability, governance, and democratic obligations.
